title: Israel election: Netanyahu-led bloc holds lead with nearly 90% of votes counted
summary: With nearly 90% of votes counted, the pro-Netanyahu bloc is just ahead of the anti-Netanyahu bloc, but neither grouping is expected to win a majority, with tough coalition talks ahead. Follow DW.
byline: Patrick Große, Mark Hallam, Felix Tamsut, Roshni Majumdar, Matt Ford

image.caption: Both Netanyahu (L) and Eisenkot (R) have said they're ready to form a government, but neither of their coalitions controls a majority of seatsImage: J. Samad/AFP/G. Cohen-Magen/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: UN rights chief: Next government should 'change course massively'

blocks.caption: Volker Türk said he hoped a new Israeli government would drastically change its courseImage: Marwan Naamani/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: The United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights, Volker Türk, told reporters in New York that he hopes a new Israeli government will "change course massively" and respect international law.

"The message is: don't continue the current course of warfare where you think you are above international law, because I think that's what we have frankly seen in the current environment," Türk said, as relayed by the AFP news agency.

"Israel has its obligations under international law, international humanitarian law, international human rights law, and they need to respect them," he said. "And I hope that the next government will do precisely that and change course massively."
Türk also said in a statement on Monday that Israel's operation in recent days in the occupied West Bank city of Hebron raised serious concerns about "unnecessary and disproportionate" use of force.
He said that more than 2,000 people had been displaced, with homes and commercial property destroyed and free movement impeded by the lockdown.
"Collective punishment is a grave violation of international law," Türk said. "Threats to empty and erase entire neighborhoods also raise serious concerns of ethnic cleansing."
